articles.headline: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning
keyFacts: The UK government stated it is working to identify and patch exposure in online services following vulnerabilities found in the PHP programming language.
Governments and major companies like Amazon scrambled to protect systems after details of the flaws leaked on social media before an official warning embargo was lifted.
Organizations worldwide applied fixes or took systems offline as advised by agencies including the UK's National Cyber Security Centre.
body: - Published

The UK government says it is working to actively identify and patch any potential exposure in its online services, after vulnerabilities were identified in the PHP programming language that underpins a significant number of the world's websites.
Governments and some of the world's biggest companies, including Amazon, were scrambling to protect their systems on Thursday before hackers could exploit them.
The flaws were first discovered by AI, after which governments and agencies urged websites to address them.
Amazon was targeted in multiple attempts, which it said occurred before an embargo on the warning was lifted. It added that it was unclear how actors knew about the vulnerabilities.
A UK government spokesperson urged "all organisations, private and public, large and small" to follow guidance to protect their systems.
The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia, earlier urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes.
"Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated," the NCSC said in a note, external.
Amazon announced on Wednesday that it had identified a "PHP2Shell exploitation attempt" that occurred on 17 October.
In the attack, an anonymous internet address attempted to target weaknesses in one of Amazon's decoy or "honeypot" systems, the company's security chief CJ Moses said.
The use of an anonymous IP address suggests that the activity was conducted by a "threat actor", he said.

While the PHP Foundation intended to release its discovery later this month along with a complete fix for the problem, usually referred to by software developers as a "patch", details of the flaw were leaked on social media on Tuesday.
In subsequent attacks on Amazon that occurred on 21 October, "the actual payloads and choices in anonymisation infrastructure varied, suggesting these were multiple actors," Moses said.
The attacks occurred after the leak, but before the embargo was lifted on the PHP warning.
The use of AI means that "more actors can act within hours or even minutes once technical details of a vulnerability are disclosed", Moses added.

The PHP incident has "demonstrated how quickly AI is changing our cybersecurity landscape", Australian Council on AI Strategy CEO Anna-Maria Arabia told the BBC, as "what used to take months, to expose a vulnerability, is now taking days".
She warned that threats would only become more commonplace as AI technology rapidly improves. It is "not going backwards, in other words", she said.
The PHP flaws went undetected for at least a decade.
Cyber-security firm Wiz has estimated that "roughly 70%" of the internet is affected, though the BBC is unable to independently verify that figure.
The Dutch cybersecurity agency went offline as a precaution, and Finland's government shut down its public web services. Wikipedia also took down parts of its website.

This was in line with advice issued by governments, including the US, to take websites down if the flaws could not immediately be fixed. PHP released software patches that could be used to address the flaws on 21 October.
The US National Security Agency said that the vulnerabilities identified, "often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database".

It could allow attackers to "steal sensitive data, disrupt services, or move deeper into a network. These vulnerabilities are flaws in PHP itself, not in the hosted application or its configuration," the NSA said in a later update.
OpenAI called the discovery, "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory".

articles.headline: UEFA Europa League Preview: Juventus vs Rennes – Team News, Lineups & Prediction
keyFacts: Juventus and Rennes will face each other at Allianz Stadium in the UEFA Europa League following weekend domestic defeats.
Juventus enters the match with a 100% record in the league phase despite multiple player injuries, including Francisco Conceicao.
Rennes travels to Italy missing Esteban Lepaul and seeking to overcome a poor away record against Serie A opponents.
body: UEFA Europa League Preview: Juventus vs Rennes – Team News, Lineups & Prediction Allianz Stadium sets the stage for a handsomely-looking UEFA Europa League clash between Juventus and Rennes. It’s a chance for both sides to put last weekend’s disappointments behind them and turn the page.

Lazio shocked Turin on Sunday, strolling to a dominant 3-0 win and heightening the pressure on head coach Luciano Spalletti. It’s been an underwhelming start to the season for Juventus, who have won just three of their last seven outings in all competitions (W3, D2, L2), though two of those three wins came in the Europa League.

After a thumping 5-0 victory over NEC Nijmegen on the opening matchday, Juventus fought back from an early deficit to beat Celta Vigo 2-1 on the road last week. As a result, they head into round three as one of just ten teams with a 100% record in this season’s league-phase campaign. However, Rennes could be a tricky opponent.

Like Juventus, Franck Haise’s side suffered defeat in their domestic championship at the weekend. Paris FC eked out a pulsating 4-3 win over Rennes in the last Ligue 1 round, knocking Les Rouge et Noirs off a two-game winning streak in all competitions. A come-from-behind 2-1 home triumph over OFI Crete in the last Europa League round was part of that run, which was a perfect response to a dull 0-0 draw at Sturm Graz on day one.
Match Preview
Juventus

Spalletti can only hope that a return to the Europa League could be a welcome distraction from Juventus’ domestic slump. The record-time Italian champions already trail Serie A pacesetters Inter by eight points and are seemingly out of the Scudetto race after just seven league rounds.

However, Juventus could salvage what promises to be another heartbreaking Serie A season with a long-awaited European success. Their last Europa League triumph came in the early 1990s, and lifting the trophy this term would provide a much-needed morale boost and restore some pride amid immense domestic struggles.

Juventus can draw confidence from winning their last four home outings in major European competitions, their longest such run since December 2021. Furthermore, the Bianconeri have won both previous meetings with Rennes, securing a 4-2 aggregate victory in the 1999 UEFA Intertoto Cup final.

Visiting Italian clubs spells disaster for Rennes, who have lost all four previous away clashes against Serie A opposition. Yet, the visitors’ promising Europa League start, highlighted by remarkable defensive discipline, suggests they could buck that trend on Thursday despite long odds.

Haise’s men lead the competition this season for the lowest expected goals against (0.79) and fewest shots faced (13). Another solid defensive performance may be vital as Rennes bid to overcome notorious inconsistency (W2, D1, L2) and put a woeful three-game winless away streak to an end (D1, L2).

It’s worth noting that Les Rouge et Noirs failed to get on the scoresheet in two of those three winless outings. Moreover, despite their impressive defensive exploits at the start of this season’s league phase, the French side conceded at least three goals in four of their last six away games in all competitions (W1, D1, L4).
Team News

Diminutive winger Francisco Conceicao dislocated his shoulder against Lazio, joining long-term absentees Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Jeff Ekhator, Kamil Grabara, and captain Manuel Locatelli on the sidelines. With the Portuguese star ruled out, Kerim Alajbegovic could make another start for Juventus, with Nick Woltemade expected to lead the line ahead of Randal Kolo Muani.

Meanwhile, French forward Esteban Lepaul remains Rennes’ only missing player ahead of this trip. Lepaul’s absence could make room for Lazio loanee Boulaye Dia to partner up with Ludovic Blas and Issa Soumare in attack.
Juventus vs Rennes Potential Starting Lineups
Juventus (3-4-2-1): Vicario; Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly; Celik, Luiz, Sarr, Cambiaso; McKennie, Alajbegovic; Woltemade.
Rennes (4-3-3): Samba; Reynolds, Cresswell, Ait Boudlal, Nagida; Szymanski, Rongier, Camara; Blas, Dia, Soumare.
Juventus vs Rennes Prediction

Spalletti is running out of excuses and can’t afford another slip-up if he’s to solidify his position in the dugout. Despite lacking several first-team stars, Juventus head into proceedings as favorites to continue their flawless Europa League start and return to winning ways against travel-sick Rennes.
Both sides have demonstrated their capacity to score in abundance so far, suggesting a high-scoring contest could be on the cards as well.

articles.headline: Takeaways for UCLA's 100-53 exhibition win over California Baptist
keyFacts: UCLA defeated California Baptist 100-53 in an exhibition basketball game on Wednesday.
Eric Dailey Jr. scored 25 points, making seven of nine three-point attempts for UCLA.
Freshman Nikola Kusturica contributed 10 points, eight rebounds, six assists, five steals, and two blocks.
body: It was quite the debut for the 2026-2027 UCLA Bruins men’s basketball team, with the season getting underway with an exhibition game against California Baptist on Wednesday. UCLA picked up a 100-53 win in a dominant showing for Mick Cronin’s team .
On the Dailey

For UCLA to compete at the top of the Big Ten Conference, the team will need some returners to take the next step. One of those returners is Eric Dailey Jr. , who played perhaps his best game as a Bruin. Dailey scored 25 points while hitting seven of his nine three point attempts.
UCLA debut for Nikola Kusturica

Serbian freshman Nikola Kusturica lived up to the hype too, scoring 10 points but showcasing his all-around game. Kusturica added eight rebounds, six assists with five steals and two blocks. If Kusturica doesn’t have to immediately take on the burden of the team’s primary scorer, he will excel as UCLA’s 17-year old jack-of-all-trades.

articles.headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo takes accountability for the Heat's loss in the season opener
keyFacts: Giannis Antetokounmpo accepted responsibility for the Miami Heat losing 131-106 to the Minnesota Timberwolves in their 2026-27 season opener.
Anthony Edwards led the Timberwolves with 45 points and 10 rebounds while Giannis scored 35 points for the Heat.
Giannis stated that his and the team's effort must improve to prevent similar losses moving forward.
body: In the 2026 offseason, the Miami Heat made a big addition by trading for Giannis Antetokounmpo. They added a superstar to a good team, which has made them one of the favorites in the Eastern Conference.

They had a good preseason, but they started the 2026-27 season with a loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves. As the star player, Giannis has taken accountability for the loss, as he wants to set the tone for the team.
Giannis Antetokounmpo shoulders the blame for the Heat losing their first game

It was a bad game for the Heat as they lost in a blowout, 131-106. The Timberwolves utterly dominated the game, as Anthony Edwards dominated with 45 points and 10 rebounds. LaMelo Ball supported him with 21 points of his own.
For the Heat, Giannis delivered because he had a 35-point performance. However, the rest of the team struggled to contain the Timberwolves' firepower.

As the superstar and one of the Heat's leaders, Antetokounmpo has personally taken on the responsibility for the loss. He does not want to see it happen again, which is why he's making sure to speak on the issues from the first loss.

"Our effort gotta be way better. It starts with me; my effort gotta be better. Our effort was not as good as it was in the past. I have to be better; it starts with me. I have to set the tone," Antetokounmpo said after the season opener loss.

With the team's struggles being apparent, Giannis wants to resolve it as soon as possible. The Heat want to compete for the championship, so if they manage to take care of these issues, they will be golden.

articles.headline: Familiar faces, new places: Grading debuts for Giannis Antetokounmpo, Kawhi Leonard, other NBA stars
keyFacts: NBA star players debuted with their new teams on Wednesday night following an eventful offseason.
Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 35 points in the Heat's 25-point season-opening loss to the Timberwolves.
Anthony Davis scored 34 points and grabbed 12 rebounds in the Wizards' 128-116 win over the Bucks.
body: After three games on Tuesday night, the rest of the NBA teams opened their 2026-27 seasons on Wednesday night. And with it, we finally got a look at a host of star players with their new teams in regular-season action on the heels of a rather eventful summer across the league.
After , here are the report cards for some other notables after their first games in different digs.
Giannis Antetokounmpo: B-

The biggest name to change teams this offseason (non-LeBron division). Once again, Pat Riley got his man. But even after acquiring Antetokounmpo, Riley hinted that they were still looking to add another major piece, indicating that the Heat needed to improve a roster that could clearly use more floor spacing, shot creators, scoring and depth.

in the Heat's ugly 25-point home loss to the Timberwolves in the season opener. Antetokounmpo had 35 points in 30 minutes, but that still wasn't enough to keep the Heat in the game. To the extent that there were any positives for Miami, at least Giannis looked like Giannis -- including airballing a free throw and being a problem in the open court (especially when the refs were lenient with traveling violations; more on that in a moment when we get to LaMelo Ball's debut).

Antetokounmpo played just 36 games in his final season with the Bucks, the result of a combination of injuries and a late-season tank job. But prior to that, he finished in the top five in the MVP voting in seven straight seasons. He'll be 32 in December, but the Heat are betting he's healthy and has plenty of top-tier basketball still to offer.
They'll need all the heavy lifting he can muster if Miami wants to join the contenders in the loaded Eastern Conference.
LaMelo Ball: C

The "C" stands for comedy. Look, there's no denying that Ball is a skilled basketball player. In an easy win over the Heat, Ball had 21 points (on 7-for-17 shooting, including 5-for-13 from deep) and six assists.

He looked comfortable next to Anthony Edwards, who went off for a game-high 45 points without breaking much of a sweat. Ball can hit shots from all over the court and he's a fantastic passer. But there's also a reason why the Hornets moved on from Ball, and they were right to do so. During his time in Charlotte, he demonstrated tantalizing talent, but that often came in the service of individual highlights and at the expense of team success. And while he made jaw-dropping plays with the Hornets, he also frequently left you scratching your head.
About that last part, just look at this. What are we doing here?

It's not so much that Ball took, oh, all the steps after his gather in what was pretty plainly an egregious travel that went uncalled. It's more that he couldn't help laughing about it and pointing to the crowd afterward, as though he'd just drained an impressive bucket. With Ball, it's impossible to be sure if he's in on the joke or completely unaware that he's doing a bit at all times.

The thinking on acquiring Ball and playing him with Edwards seems to be something on the order of the Wolves weren't going to get past the Thunder and Spurs as previously constituted, so why not give this experiment a chance? That's a hot take to be sure. Now we'll see whether the Wolves can handle it or if they eventually get burned.
Kawhi Leonard: B+

Following what we'll charitably label an eventful final year in Los Angeles, Leonard is back in Toronto. He's an instant upgrade over Brandon Ingram at both ends of the floor, and when paired with Scottie Barnes, the Raptors now boast two of the best two-way wings in the league.

His first game back with his old club didn't put too much of a strain on Leonard. He should thank the Bulls for not putting up too many roadblocks for his reentry. In a blowout 135-92 home win, Leonard had 23 points, six rebounds, two assists, four steals and a block in just 24 minutes. He shot only 5-for-17 from the floor but made all 11 of his free throws.
He was also indirectly responsible for the highlight of the night.
Anthony Davis: A

Remember him? After being traded from the Lakers back in February 2025, Davis has played just 29 games -- all of them in Dallas. When the Mavericks flipped him to the Wizards last season, Davis was true to his nickname and stayed in street clothes without stepping on the floor for Washington. Until Wednesday.

In a 128-116 win over the Bucks, Davis reminded everyone just how good he is, going for 34 points, 12 rebounds, four assists, two steals and a block. He made 11 of 20 shots and hit a 3-pointer. Best of all, he played 34 minutes. Yes, it was against the Bucks, who figure to be awful this season, but AD didn't make the schedule and knocking the rust off against Milwaukee isn't the worst thing given how long it's been since he played.

Since arriving in Washington, Davis has been a popular trade candidate in rumors and whispers around the league. The Wizards have insisted they are not interested in moving him, despite putting contract extension negotiations on hold this summer. It's hard to blame the organization for wanting to see how he fits first -- and how much he'll even be available -- before committing big money to him. Davis's talent is undeniable, but he'll be 34 in March and a litany of injuries over the course of his career has repeatedly kept him on the sidelines. He's played 56 games or fewer in six of the last 10 seasons.
But hey, at least he was out there on Wednesday, playing with Trae Young and the Wizards. The crowd seemed to appreciate it.
You know the old saying, "smoke 'em if you got 'em?" This was the "chant it while he's actually playing" basketball equivalent.
Ja Morant: A
When the Trail Blazers traded for Morant, the nearly universal question became "how is that going to work?" In the opener, the answer was "pretty well."

According to a report in The Athletic in early October, new Blazers coach Micah Nori didn't believe it made sense to start Damian Lillard and Morant in the same backcourt. That thinking didn't even last through the first game.

The Blazers started Morant on Wednesday in a runaway 124-83 home win over the Suns. In 23 minutes, Morant went for 14 points (on 6-for-8 shooting), five rebounds, eight assists and three steals with just one turnover. It's the smallest of sample sizes, but the Blazers will obviously take it.

The main concern with adding Morant was that Portland already had an overcrowded backcourt with Lillard, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson and Shaedon Sharpe (who is expected to miss extended time with a knee injury). The situation was further complicated by the Blazers unlocking Deni Avdija last season and realizing the team worked better when the offense ran through him. Throwing another high-usage player like Morant into the mix seemed inadvisable, especially when he's used to having the ball in his hands and isn't a good shooter (31.1% from deep for his career).
Against the Suns, Morant hit a pair of threes. Even more encouraging, he showed the kind of effort the Blazers will need from him if this odd mix is going to work over the course of a long season.

articles.headline: All party members in Final Fantasy Resonance
keyFacts: Final Fantasy Resonance features eight party members that players recruit by progressing through the main campaign story.
Combat parties are limited to four characters, and each character has pre-determined stat progression suited to specific roles.
All characters earn experience points and mastery points after battle regardless of whether they are in the active party.
body: Meeting new party members in Final Fantasy Resonance is part of the journey. As in other games in the series, you start with only a few characters who team up to go on an adventure, but as they progress, they make friends who join the group. Although you can only use up to four characters in combat, unlocking all available party members broadens your strategic options.
To help you navigate this adventure and locate the new allies you need to save the world, we prepared this guide to explain where to find all party members in Final Fantasy Resonance.
[Ed. note: The following guide contains light spoilers for Final Fantasy Resonance, so continue at your own risk!]
All party members in Final Fantasy Resonance

In Final Fantasy Resonance, there are eight party members that you recruit by completing the segment of the main story where you meet them. This means that they are locked behind the campaign, leaving you no alternative but to focus on completing the chapters to add new characters to your roster.

Each character belongs to a specific role, which helps you balance support and offense within your party. At the same time, using the right Vision and mastery bonus skills allows you to complement a character's kit. Shifting them to a different role is quite difficult, though, because a character's stat progression is pre-determined, they will inevitably perform better in certain roles. For example, magic attack is Sakura's highest attribute, making her a natural caster.

Final Fantasy Resonance is designed to resemble older traditional Final Fantasy games, but when it comes to character progression, you don't need to worry about leveling up characters and who is out of the main party. All characters earn both experience points and mastery points after battle.

articles.headline: Kansas Senate candidate Adam Hamilton admits ‘mistakes were made’ in church sexual abuse scandal
keyFacts: Kansas Senate candidate Adam Hamilton admitted during a debate that he made a mistake by failing to bar a volunteer accused of sexual abuse from a 2006 church retreat.
Incumbent Republican Sen. Roger Marshall launched late-campaign attacks against Hamilton over the church sexual abuse scandal involving convicted sex offender Scott Moore.
Moore was convicted in 2013 after teenagers from Hamilton's church testified against him regarding incidents that occurred in 2005 and 2006.
body: Kansas Democrat Adam Hamilton admitted during a testy Senate debate Wednesday night that he made a “mistake” by failing to bar a volunteer accused of sexual abuse in 2005 from a retreat where he allegedly abused another boy.

Hamilton, a Methodist pastor who runs Kansas’ largest church, is facing late-campaign attacks from incumbent Republican Sen. Roger Marshall over now-convicted sex offender Scott Moore, who was accused of molesting teenage boys at church retreats in 2005 and 2006.

The Democratic challenger said an internal review of allegations from two boys in 2005 was “inconclusive” and that police later found the same, but that he still believes Moore should not have been allowed to return to the church in 2006.
“I was actually preaching that weekend at Church of the Resurrection, and I did not sign off on him going back. I should have checked to make sure that he wasn’t going back,” Hamilton said.

“That was a mistake on my part. But I will tell you, when he was investigated the next year, we forbade him from working with youth or children anymore. He left our church angry and upset. And again, we played a critical role several years later in getting him arrested and convicted.”

Moore was convicted in 2013 of misdemeanor sexual battery for inappropriately touching his son’s friend at a sleepover in 2010. Teenagers from Hamilton’s church who alleged abuse in 2005 and 2006 testified against him.
In November 2005, a 15-year-old boy alleged that Moore touched his penis and a 14-year-old said Moore reached inside his sleeping bag at an overnight retreat.
Prosecutors later wrote in court documents that the two victims provided “detailed” statements to church officials, but weren’t able to positively identify Moore at the time.

He returned as a volunteer in November 2006 and allegedly inappropriately touched a 15-year-old boy. The church informed the Linn County Sheriff’s Office, but the county attorney’s office didn’t pursue charges.
Hamilton told the Kansas Reflector in July he “absolutely” would handle things differently in retrospect, but that “there was no attempt at a cover-up.”

The candidate told CNN’s Jake Tapper on Tuesday that “it was not completely clear what had happened at the time [in 2005] and who exactly had done this thing” and that Moore “should have never been there [in 2006]. These were mistakes that were made.”
Marshall also answered for late-breaking attacks, including over reportedly suing 700 patients of his medical practice for unpaid bills.
Marshall said that litigation decisions were “out of our hands” after unpaid bills were turned over to collections agencies and said it was the “same practice” other doctors and hospitals use.

The Kansas Senate race is close, according to the latest polls, as Hamilton positions himself as a moderate Democrat, criticizing former President Joe Biden’s border policies and disapproving of the rising socialist wing of the party.

articles.headline: What is PHP and why did it spark a global cyber-security scramble?
keyFacts: Researchers used artificial intelligence to uncover severe vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language that had gone undetected for over a decade.
Governments and cyber-security agencies globally scrambled to contain the fallout, urging website operators to install emergency patches or take vulnerable platforms offline.
Experts warned that more attempts to exploit the flaws are likely in the coming weeks as technical details become public.
body: - Published
For more than a decade, serious flaws had gone undetected in technology underpinning much of the internet.
It took artificial intelligence (AI) to bring them to light and caused a global cyber-security alert.
The vulnerabilities lie within a programming language called PHP, which has been used internationally since the 2000s to build websites.

Governments and cyber-security agencies around the world scrambled to contain the fallout of this discovery on Wednesday, and have urged website operators to install a new emergency fix or consider taking their platforms offline.
Cyber-security firm Wiz - one of the companies whose researchers uncovered the vulnerabilities - described the flaws as the "most severe" ever detected by AI.
OpenAI, whose technology was used to find the flaws, called the discovery "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory".
What is the flaw?
Most people may not have heard of PHP - short for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor - but they most certainly interact with it daily.
PHP powers a vast number of platforms, including online shops, Wikipedia and WordPress â the content management system behind many websites like blogs.

When you visit a website like Wikipedia, PHP is the code that collects information you need and presents it in a way you can read on the web, Paul Spain, chief executive of Gorilla Cyber Security, told the BBC.
But due to a flaw that could allow attackers to take control of affected web servers without authentication and steal sensitive data, everything built on PHP was left exposed.
AI could make such attacks easier and faster, Spain said, estimating that the flaw could affect "millions and millions" of websites.
It would be "disastrous" if hackers or countries weaponised the flaw and seized private data from websites, said cyber-security researcher Jill Slay from the University of Adelaide.
What websites have been affected?
The alert has disrupted services globally, from gaming platforms to government portals and online forums.
That includes Wikimedia - the organisation behind the online encyclopaedia Wikipedia - which took down a number of its systems as a precautionary measure.
Sites and pages have been taken offline by the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC, with the Netherlands' cyber-security agency also pulling its website.
A number of Scotland's public organisations, including councils and health boards, have also taken their websites offline.
Some experts warn the vulnerability could leave poorly maintained websites, particularly those belonging to smaller organisations with limited security resources, at greater risk.
More attempts to exploit these flaws are likely in the coming weeks since the technical details are now being made public, cyber-security researcher Salil Kanhere from UNSW Sydney said.
What happened after the flaws were exposed?
Developers of the PHP platform on Wednesday rolled out patches to fix the vulnerabilities that had been lurking in their software for years.
"All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately," the company said.
Authorities and security organisations around the world have echoed those warnings to website operators to secure their platforms.

The US National Security Agency told all organisations that use PHP to take their systems offline if they were unable to patch them immediately, adding that the flaw could provide a "direct path" to exploit a system's database.
"These risks are serious enough to require immediate patching across United States Government departments and agencies," the agency said.
The UK's National Cyber Security Centre gave similar advice and told organisations to check for "backdoors installed by an attacker".
Its counterparts in the EU and Australia have also issued similar alerts.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged people to check if their publicly available websites ran on PHP.
"We have an urgent request for everyone to take action tonight," Takaichi wrote on X.
"If it is difficult to apply the fix patch promptly, temporarily suspending websites and similar measures can be considered an effective way to reduce risk," she said.
How is AI finding weak spots?
The vulnerabilities were found by researchers at the security firms Calif and Wiz.
The researchers used advanced AI tools that are able to analyse code and find flaws much faster than humans or older systems can.
"Modern software is incredibly complex, and some vulnerabilities can remain undetected for years," Kanhere said.
"The underlying bugs weren't new; what changed was our ability to find them," Kanhere said.
Details of the discovery leaked online this week, forcing the PHP platform's developers to rush out its announcement of the security flaw and its huge scale.
The incident "highlights how AI can uncover security flaws" but also how it can "help attackers rapidly develop offensive tools and exploits," OpenAI said in a blog post.
The ChatGPT-maker said it had released a program to check if the PHP platform is secure.

"Many of these flaws stem from the way software were built in the past, which were built for functionality and not with security in mind," said Ryan Ko, at the University of Queensland's Cyber Research Centre.
What can people do to safeguard themselves?
Website owners are being urged to secure their websites with the latest version of PHP.
The US National Security Agency has urged "heightened awareness" in the coming weeks and to closely monitor updates from software vendors.
"Vigilance in applying patches related to those systems is paramount," it said.
The onus lies mainly on website operators, but users should stay alert for any security advice issued by affected services, such as requests to change passwords, Kanhere said.
He warned people to be alert to any phishing messages exploiting the publicity around the incident too.

articles.headline: History comes home as St Louis City top Columbus Crew to win US Open Cup
keyFacts: St Louis City won the US Open Cup by defeating the Columbus Crew 5-4 on penalties after a scoreless match, ending a 38-year wait for a major US soccer title.
Daniel Edelman scored the decisive penalty kick, and backup goalkeeper Ben Lundt made a crucial save after starter Roman Bürki left the match on a stretcher due to an injury.
The victory earned St Louis City a spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup and marked the club's first major trophy under MLS's youngest manager, Yoann Damet.
body: For much of the 20th century, winning the US Open Cup required a team to beat someone from St Louis. The Gateway City was home to many of the nation’s best teams during some ramshackle eras of soccer in the United States, with six different clubs combining for 10 trophy lifts. The most recent came in 1988, when St Louis Busch Seniors beat San Francisco-based Greek-American AC in the last throes of a tournament history dominated by amateur and semi-pro teams. MLS has won every Open Cup but one since starting play in 1996, and St Louis didn’t have an MLS club until 2023.

From the beginning, club figures spoke of aims to restore the city to soccer prominence. Well, mission accomplished. St Louis City are US Open Cup champions, outlasting the Columbus Crew 5-4 on penalties away from home to end the city’s 38-year wait for a major US soccer title and earn a place in the field for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup.
Daniel Edelman scored the decisive penalty, with backup goalkeeper Ben Lundt making a save on Columbus’ first attempt, himself having entered the match in the second half.

Fittingly given their home city’s rich soccer history, City’s first trophy is also the nation’s oldest. Wednesday marked the 109th final in the history of the Open Cup, which was first held in 1913–14 and has run continuously save for a two-year hiatus during the Covid-19 pandemic.

However, St Louis did so with MLS’s youngest manager – Yoann Damet, the 36-year-old Frenchman who was previously Wilfried Nancy’s top assistant in Columbus but was passed over for the top job after Nancy left. St Louis will be thankful that he was.

Often two of the nation’s most aesthetically pleasing teams, Columbus and St Louis opened the final by minimizing risk. For the opening half-hour, St Louis carried a 60% share of possession but failed to muster a single shot. The hosts were a bit more incisive whenever they found the ball, working to advance upfield and trying to fashion chances for Brais Méndez, but failed to threaten Roman Bürki’s net.
Referee Guido Gonzales Jr promptly blew his half-time whistle after the 45th minute. No need for stoppage time after that half, and few could argue.

Both teams returned with intentions to sustain the caginess after the break. Columbus continued to dramatically tilt the field, taking 11 touches in St Louis’ box after half-time before the visitors managed a single one. Still, Bürki kept their sole on-target effort from rippling the net. The visitors responded by upping their fouling volume to further impede the Crew’s efforts.

The 69th minute provided an inflection point as Columbus again entered the St Louis box, where Santi Rodríguez took a clattering from behind by Carlo Holse but saw the referee play the advantage. Méndez picked up the loose ball, strafed across the top of the box to his left, and played a through-ball to former Morocco international Anass Zaroury, whose shot was blocked by a fearless Bürki who took contact to his head from the wing-back’s knee, staying down as the play fizzled.

As the former Switzerland international received medical treatment, the VAR had ample time to review and, ultimately, clear the potential penalty on Holse’s initial tackle. Ultimately, a six-minute examination led to Bürki exiting the match on a stretcher, leaving to a stadium-wide applause. Later, the CBS Sports broadcast relayed that Bürki was “OK” shortly after his departure, though he was taken to the hospital for an evaluation. In stepped Lundt, a backup since coming to MLS in 2019 – but one who had played shootout hero before for St Louis, winning their quarter-final shootout against Houston.

Another injury, seemingly a leg muscle issue to promising Columbus midfielder Taha Habroune, brought Eric Bailly off the bench with captain Sean Zawadzki pushing into midfield to accommodate. The fourth official showed 11 minutes of stoppage time, perhaps cashing some rollover minutes from the first half on top of the lengthy delay as Bürki was examined. The Nordecke increased the volume of their support, but the game’s established physicality hardly waned for their efforts. St Louis seemed to fashion a clear look inside the box in the 10th minute of stoppage time, but US international Damion Downs took too heavy a touch to fashion a shot.

A minute later, the whistle blew. Despite Columbus outshooting St Louis 16-3, both teams finished the 90 minutes without a goal to their name or a trophy to their claim. Another 30 minutes of brawling followed.
Neither team ceded an inch in the opening minutes of extra time, exchanging hard challenges and failing to maximize their ensuing set pieces.

After Timo Baumgartl started the sequence with a make, Columbus’ Santi Rodriguez sent his attempt to Lundt’s left only to be stifled by a strong left hand. The teams each converted their next three attempts, although Lundt nearly ended the sequence with a finger to Andrés Herrera’s effort in the fourth round. Edelman stepped up and made no mistake with his trophy-winner.

The MLS schedule-makers did the finalists no favors as both teams played on the road this weekend, although St Louis enjoyed an extra day of rest. St Louis also entered the final at a known disadvantage, playing without striker Rafael Navarro. A front-runner for the year-end MLS Best XI, Navarro played for the Colorado Rapids through the quarter-final stage, cap-tying him for the remainder of the tournament.

While Columbus was recently a contender on all fronts under Nancy, his departure at the end of 2025 forced the Crew into a stylistic reset. Rather than hire his top assistant, Damet, Columbus looked beyond the league and hired Henrik Rydström, a self-proclaimed acolyte of “relationism”. The Swede never adapted to MLS, quickly leading Columbus toward the bottom of the East before being shown the door in May after just 17 matches.

His replacement, Laurent Courtois, was another Nancy disciple. Meanwhile, Damet is a frontrunner for coach of the year, is in line for a top-three finish in the Western Conference – and, now, is the Open Cup champion.

In an era where fiction fixates on multiverses, Columbus will no doubt wonder what could have been had they opted for continuity and retained Damet. Their loss is St Louis’ gain, as the Western Conference club will hope this is the first of multiple trophies to be won under MLS’s youngest manager.

articles.headline: Kansas Senate rivals distance themselves from party leaders in fiery debate
keyFacts: Republican Senator Roger Marshall and Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton distanced themselves from party leaders during a contentious Kansas Senate debate.
Both candidates addressed personal controversies involving Marshall's former medical practice lawsuits and Hamilton's handling of camp safety allegations.
Marshall and Hamilton clashed over national issues including Donald Trump's agenda, immigration, and Senate control.
body: Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., and Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton repeatedly sought to distance themselves from the most unpopular elements of their respective parties Wednesday night during a contentious Kansas Senate debate.
Both candidates battled over President Donald Trump, immigration, the war in Iran and more in a race that could help determine control of the Senate.
The debate opened on a personal note, with both candidates pressed over controversies that have fueled attack ads in the closing weeks of the campaign.

Marshall was questioned about a New York Times review that found his former medical practice sued more than 700 patients over unpaid bills. The Republican defended the practice while emphasizing the millions of dollars in free care his practice provided.
GOP SENATOR ALLEGES SCHUMER BEHIND 'HIT JOB' REPORT ON FORMER PATIENTS
"Every year we gave away $3 to $4 million of charity, but we also had a business," Marshall said. "We had 300 employees, we had a mortgage payment, we had electric."

Hamilton, meanwhile, was questioned about his handling of allegations involving a volunteer at his church's summer camp alleged to have been a sexual predator. Hamilton acknowledged that he should have ensured the individual did not return to the camp after an initial investigation.
"I should have checked to make sure that he wasn't going back," Hamilton said. "That was a mistake on my part."
The candidates spent much of the rest of the debate trying to define each other by their respective national parties.

Marshall repeatedly warned that electing Hamilton would help hand control of the Senate to Democrats and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer , while Hamilton sought to portray himself as an independent-minded Democrat willing to break with his party.
THE NINE KEY RACES THAT WILL DECIDE WHO CONTROLS THE SENATE, AND WHERE THEY STAND
That divide came into focus when the moderator played footage of Trump campaigning for Marshall in Kansas earlier this week and telling voters to "pretend, please, that I'm on the ballot."
Asked whether that meant he would support every part of Trump's agenda, Marshall said no and pointed to recent disagreements involving immigration enforcement in southwest Kansas and beef imports.
"Just like with my wife, I can disagree with her. My wife is always right," Marshall joked. "And President Trump is not always right."
Nevertheless, Marshall emphasized his support for much of Trump's agenda and urged the president's supporters to turn out for him.

"We need the Trump voters to come out," Marshall said. "If you want the Trump agenda to continue, if you want secure borders, if you want a strong military, if you want lower taxes, then you — and you voted for President Trump — you need to come out."
Hamilton faced a similar challenge when moderators pressed him over his past support for Democrats and his campaign message of "leading from the middle."
MANCHIN CALLS SCHUMER 'CRAZY' FOR TRYING TO OUST GOP SENATOR IN CRUCIAL SENATE SHOWDOWN
The Democratic nominee explicitly broke with former President Joe Biden over immigration.
"The Biden policies when it came to the border were a disaster," Hamilton said. "I believe in strong and secure borders."
Hamilton also said he would not support Schumer for majority leader if Democrats win control of the Senate.
The debate did produce an unusual moment of agreement when both candidates were asked how many genders there are.
"There's two. There's a boy and there's a girl," Marshall said.
"There are two genders, male and female," Hamilton responded.
SC DEM SENATE CANDIDATE CLAIMS SHE WILL STAND UP TO HER PARTY AS GRAHAM TIES HER TO 'SOCIALIST DEMOCRATS'

Hamilton later said he did not want biological males competing against his 12-year-old granddaughter in sports, calling it "not a fair fight," while arguing that decisions over athletic participation should generally be handled locally rather than by the federal government.

The Kansas contest has emerged as an unexpectedly competitive Senate race in the closing weeks of the midterms . Marshall is seeking a second term in a state that has not elected a Democratic U.S. senator since 1932, while Hamilton, a longtime pastor, has campaigned as a moderate Democrat.
Trump traveled to Kansas Monday to campaign for Marshall as Republicans work to defend the seat with control of the Senate at stake.

articles.headline: Philippine government suspends top tech official for alleged misconduct
keyFacts: The Philippines Ombudsman suspended DICT Undersecretary David L. Almirol for six months without pay over alleged misconduct regarding government contracts.
The Ombudsman alleged that the DICT awarded at least eight contracts worth over ₱1.5 billion to entities linked to Almirol's former company, Multisys.
The Ombudsman stated the suspension is a precautionary measure to prevent Almirol from interfering with the ongoing investigation.
body: The Philippines government’s Ombudsman has suspended a senior Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) official over allegations he assigned government contracts to a company he founded and continued to hold a stake in.

The Ombudsman announced the suspension yesterday and named Undersecretary for E-Government David L. Almirol as the individual of concern, after considering “administrative complaints of Grave Misconduct, Conduct Prejudicial to the Best Interest of the Service and violation of … the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees.”
“In ordering the preventive suspension, the Ombudsman found strong evidence supporting the administrative charges against Almirol,” according to its announcement of the suspension.

Almirol founded a company called Multisys Technologies Corporation that offers software development services, plus packaged products. After over a decade as the company’s CEO, Almirol in 2022 joined DICT at the request of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., to work on improving e-government services.

The Ombudsman alleged that between 2023 and 2025 DICT awarded at least eight contracts valued at over ₱1.5 billion ($24 million) to entities linked with Multisys. The contracts covered information and communications technology consultancy, e-government application deployment, web-based messaging services, cloud infrastructure, data center colocation and software subscriptions. Evidence of those transactions is apparently on the record in Multisys’s books.

Local laws mean Almirol should have divested his stake in Multisys within 60 days. The Ombudsman alleges the exec missed that deadline but later complied. It’s not alleged he issued contracts in the period during which he continued to hold Multisys shares.

The Ombudsman has suspended Almirol without pay for six months, a step it says is necessary because if he continued in the role it “could prejudice the investigation, particularly given his control and custody of documents and evidence relevant to the case.”

The org has also pointed out that its decision does not pre-judge the matter, but is “a precautionary measure intended to preserve the integrity of the proceedings and ensure an impartial and unimpeded investigation.”

President Marcos Jr. made rooting out corruption a key plank of his platform and even created an agency to tackle the problem. However, it’s felt that some anti-corruption actions may have been partly politically motivated.
Past tech-related scandals in the Philippines include a 2022 case that saw its Department of Education overpay for lousy laptops . ®

articles.headline: Ilhan Omar vacating DC apartment after federal raid, citing death threats
keyFacts: Rep. Ilhan Omar announced Wednesday that she is vacating her Washington, D.C., apartment due to death threats following a federal investigation.
Federal investigators recently raided Omar's home and seized 17 items, which she said is part of a politically motivated conspiracy against her.
The ongoing federal investigation involves probes into Omar's financial records and allegations of a fraudulent marriage for U.S. residency.
body: Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN) on Wednesday said she will be forced to move away from her Washington, D.C., apartment because of death threats she said she received after becoming the subject of a federal investigation.

Omar has been the subject of government investigations for months. President Donald Trump said in January that the Department of Justice was probing Omar over discrepancies in her financial records. Vice President JD Vance later revealed that the DOJ is also investigating allegations that Omar participated in a sham marriage with her biological brother from Somalia so he could gain residency in the United States.

After federal investigators raided Omar’s home in Washington, D.C., earlier this month, seizing her cellphone, notebooks, personal computers, and passport, the congresswoman said this week that she had to vacate the residence. During an interview on MS Now, Omar proclaimed her innocence, saying she would “stand up to the bullies.”

“Obviously, I can’t continue to live there. … Because our address has been public and with the death threats that I deal with, it’s no longer going to be feasible to be in that house and have my kids visiting off and on, having people track them,” she said.
“If I continue to live my truth, if I continue to fight for the right things, if I continue to stand up to bullies and people who are carrying out ungodly corruption, I’m going to be OK,” Omar added.

The government’s investigation into Omar, who is originally from Somalia, appears to be based on concerns that she and her family lied on key paperwork about her age and other details in order to gain legal residency in the U.S. decades ago. The immigration fraud case could end in her denaturalization and deportation if the Trump administration were successful at proving such claims.
Omar has denounced the investigations as a politically motivated conspiracy against her, and used it to urge supporters to donate to her reelection campaign.
ILHAN OMAR DEPORTATION CASE COMPLICATED BY PROCEDURAL FACTORS

On Wednesday, she said up to 15 Homeland Security Investigations agents executed a search warrant earlier this month at her home as part of the investigation. They took 17 items, including several phones, according to Omar.

“You don’t show up to somebody’s house that early in the morning unless you’re trying to freak them out,” the Democratic lawmaker said. “Obviously, they’d like to see me locked up, deported, and all of those things. But I think the bigger satisfaction for them would be for me to be like, ‘I’m tired of all of you, and I’m going to leave.'”

articles.headline: Austrian, Swiss women kidnapped in Niger are freed — report
keyFacts: Niger released an Austrian woman and a Swiss woman after more than a year in captivity, according to reports.
The freed women were flown to Benghazi, Libya, and thanked Libyan military leaders Khalifa Haftar and his son Saddam for their release.
Austrian and Swiss authorities identified the hostages as Eva G. and Claudia Abbt, who were abducted in Niger in 2025.
body: Niger released two women, one Swiss and the other Austrian, after over a year of holding them captive, according to multiple reports.
The two women were flown out to Libya's eastern city of Benghazi, Libyan media outlets reported on Thursday.
The Austrian national, identified by Austrian authorities as Eva G., and the Swiss national, whom the Swiss foreign ministry has not previously named, were both abducted in Niger in 2025.
Eva G. is in her 70s, and the Swiss woman, identified by media outlets as Claudia Abbt, is 69 years old, according to reports.
Eva G. was kidnapped in the desert town of Agadez in central Niger, in January 2025. Abbt was abducted in April 2025.
It was not immediately clear which group was holding them and what demands it had made.
Libyan news channel releases video of the two women freed from captivity
In a video released by Libya's al-Masar TV, the women appeared physically weakened.
Both women thanked the deputy commander-in-chief of Libya's armed forces, Khalifa Haftar, and his son, Saddam, for their release. Haftar reportedly oversaw the operation that freed the women.
"I had been held hostage for a year and nine months," Eva G. said, while Abbt said she was "happy to be free," also thanking Haftar.

Libya and Niger share a border hundreds of miles long, cutting through the Sahara Desert and connecting with Algeria and Chad on either side. Libya has struggled to recover from the chaos that followed the 2011 NATO-backed uprising that toppled longtime ruler Moammar Gaddafi.
At the moment, two governments are vying for power there: a UN-recognized administration led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah and its rival in the east, backed by Haftar.
Edited by: Roshni Majumdar
Editor's note: DW has not yet independently verified the video released by the Libyan news channel that shows the two women, now freed, speaking to camera.

articles.headline: Apple Limitis iPhone Duo Purchases to 2 Foldable Phones Per Person
keyFacts: Apple is limiting sales of its new iPhone Duo foldable phone to a maximum of two devices per customer.
Preorders for the iPhone Duo are currently backordered until the end of January, though limited stock will be available in stores.
The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable phone, entering a market previously contested by competitors like Samsung, Motorola, and Google.
body: If you were hoping to score multiple iPhone Duo devices from Apple when the new foldable becomes available on Friday, we have some bad news for you: The tech giant is limiting sales of the phone to two per person.

As reported earlier this week by MacRumors, when we attempted to add more than two to our bag on the Apple Store, we got the following message: “A maximum of 2 iPhone Duo can be purchased per customer. Please adjust the total quantity of iPhone Duo in your order before checking out.”
The limit of two foldables per purchase will presumably also apply to those shopping in-store when the phone finally launches on Friday.
More from CNET

While preorders are backed up until the end of January — our estimated delivery when adding two to our bag is Jan. 25, as of the time of publication — Apple will have limited stock of the iPhone Duo in stores, though you may have to wait in line overnight to be one of the few people able to get their hands on one (or two).

While companies may limit the number of devices in each order, especially for stock-scarce products like game consoles, it’s been a while since Apple has restricted how many phones people can buy at once. Nearly two decades ago, the company launched the original iPhone to great fanfare in September 2007, but limited buyers to two per order (later easing it to five by the holidays). The restriction returned in 2012, when Apple limited orders to two iPhone 5 preorders per customer.

If you do want to buy more than one iPhone Duo, we found that we could add multiple to our carts while shopping at Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile and Best Buy, though all of those purchases require you to sign up for a line of service with a carrier. Preorders are likewise back-ordered until the end of January, however.

The iPhone Duo is Apple’s first foldable phone, entering the mobile niche that Samsung and Motorola have been fighting over since 2020, with Google entering the fray with the first Pixel Fold in 2023. Chinese phonemakers like Huawei and Xiaomi have also released their own foldables, though none have been sold widely in the US.

Despite refined devices like the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, Motorola Razr Ultra 2026 and Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold releasing earlier this year, analysts predict that Apple’s new device will carve out a significant chunk of the market: The International Data Corporation expects the Duo to amount to 31% of the foldable share of the phones market by the end of the year, growing to 40% in 2027.

Customer preorders seem to have followed those predictions, though we’ll have to wait and see whether that appetite continues throughout the holidays and into the new year. Early reviews have been positive, with CNET Senior Reporter Abrar Al-Heeti noting that despite some downsides attributable to a first-generation device, the Apple foldable’s finer details make the experience feel fluid and cohesive.
“Personally, I have no plans of switching back to a slab phone anytime soon,” Al-Heeti said in her review.

articles.headline: GridCraft is the open-source Excel clone for Linux I’ve been waiting for
keyFacts: ArtCraft released GridCraft, a free and open-source spreadsheet application designed to mimic Microsoft Excel on multiple operating systems including Linux.
ZDNet reported that GridCraft runs natively in Rust, supports XLSX compatibility, and features over 500 calculation functions with fast performance.
ZDNet noted that the only major missing feature in GridCraft is a strong template system, as it currently lacks an easy way to save files as .xltx templates.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways
- GridCraft is almost the MS Excel clone it intends to be.
- GridCraft is both free and open-source.
- The only thing missing is a strong template feature.
ArtCraft, the development team behind PhotoCraft (and a number of other similar apps) reverse-engineered yet another de facto standard app: GridCraft, meant to mimic Microsoft Excel.

ArtCraft’s collection is an important step forward for open source and the Linux operating system because some of the apps they’ve built have long been considered roadblocks to user adoption of Linux. With apps like WordCraft, DeckCraft, and PDFCraft now available, those roadblocks go away. Time will tell, but these apps seem like a big step forward for Linux and open-source to me.
More from ZDNET
What does GridCraft do?

You might be thinking that this is simply a rebranded MS Excel that runs on top of an interpretation or abstraction layer, but that is not the case. Like the other ArtCraft apps, GridCraft runs natively on whatever OS you are using (Linux, FreeBSD, MacOS, or Windows). And because these apps were written in Rust, they are blazingly fast.
I’ve opened very large spreadsheets in GridCraft (one with 1,000 rows), and the app never so much as hiccuped.

GridCraft works on more platforms than Excel and is free, which are obvious perks, as is the fact that it’s released under an open license, so anyone can download the code, edit it, rebuild it, and redistribute it.
Also: How to use ChatGPT to write Excel formulas

With GridCraft, you get a standard spreadsheet workflow, native XLSX compatibility, more than 500 calculation functions, charts & pivot tables, agent-native automation, and copy-on-write workbooks with instant undo snapshots, incremental recalculation, and a virtualized grid.

I’ve tested GridCraft on Linux, MacOS, and Windows, and it performs exactly the same and as fast on every platform. So if you’re accustomed to MS Excel’s draggy performance, you’ll be pleasantly surprised with how fast GridCraft does everything. Click on the launcher, and it opens immediately.

Once opened, you can start creating your own spreadsheet from scratch. Although there are three samples (Household Budget, Quarterly Sales Dashboard, and Gradebook), the templates are lacking. You can always create your own templates or download some from the official MS Template download site.

Keep in mind that if there’s one aspect of GridCraft that differs from Excel, it’s templates. I’ve yet to find a way to save a spreadsheet as an .xltx (template) file. Hopefully, the developers will add a more robust template feature in the future. In the meantime, you can always save a spreadsheet as a CSV file into a templates folder you create. It’s a hack, but it works.
How well does GridCraft perform?

As I said, GridCraft is not exactly a 1:1 drop-in replacement for Excel. Even so, it’s pretty close and works as you would expect. It offers the same features, the same UI (minus the MS branding), and does the same calculations. I opened an Excel spreadsheet with a pivot table, and everything was in place and functioning properly.

Although I’ve tested the app on several spreadsheets without a single issue, your spreadsheet could be the one that encounters problems. Because of that, I would suggest always making a copy of your work and using the copy on GridCraft. No matter how well GridCraft performs, do not go into the app thinking it is production-ready.
Also: How I made this great-looking table in Excel
Because spreadsheets can sometimes be the heart of your business or project, you always want to make sure you have a copy of your data. I would say that for any application you use.

Will I be using it for spreadsheets? You bet I will. In fact, I’ve begun adopting all of the ArtCraft apps to replace other, similar apps I use. The one exception to that is FilmCraft, but only because I’ve invested so much time and money into DaVinci Resolve, and FilmCraft doesn’t quite have the color tools and node trees that I’m used to.

articles.headline: Ilhan Omar gives head-scratching response when asked if she’s related to ex-husband in first interview since DC raid
keyFacts: Rep. Ilhan Omar called allegations that she married her brother insane during her first interview since federal agents raided her Washington, DC, home.
Homeland Security Investigations agents raided Omar and her husband's residence last week as part of an ongoing immigration fraud investigation.
Omar denied committing immigration fraud and stated she is confident she did nothing wrong.
body: Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) on Wednesday called allegations that she married her brother “insane” – but didn’t entirely close the door to the possibility of being related to her ex-husband.
“Not to my knowledge,” Omar responded, when asked by MS NOW’s Chris Hayes if there was any “weird kernel of truth” to the claim that she wed her brother.

The decade-old allegations that Omar and her ex, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, got hitched in a failed effort to get him a green card originated on a “Somali blog,” and spread when “right-wing conspiracy theorists” latched onto it, Omar explained in her first interview since federal agents raided her Washington, DC, home last week.
“Somebody put in there that, you know, he had to have been my brother or something to that effect,” the Minnesota Democrat said.
According to Omar, bloggers “went and like found random people who are like .. ‘She introduced him to us and said he was her brother,’ which is, you know, insane.”

Omar then described herself as “working class” and living “paycheck to paycheck,” when asked about her current financial situation in light of documents where Omar suggested she and her husband had a combined net-worth of some $30 million, which she later claimed was a mistake and revised down.

“I have a Toyota Camry that’s from 2016. It’s our only car. I rent my DC place and my Minneapolis place, and so I mean, I don’t know, that sounds like not the majority of Congress, but there’s some of us that don’t come from wealth and don’t have wealth,” she told Hayes.

“I can’t continue to live there, so we have to figure out where to move to,” she said, lamenting that her address was made public and “with the death threats that I deal with, it’s no longer going to be feasible to be in that house and have my kids like visiting off and on, having people track them.”
The “Squad” congresswoman has been laying low since a search warrant was obtained and executed last Monday.

In her first on-camera remarks since the search, Omar urged her supporters to donate to her re-election campaign so she could “fight Trump and his administration for trying to intimidate me and so many other people right before the midterm elections.”
Homeland Security Investigations agents raided the residence Omar shares with her husband, Tim Mynett, as part of an investigation into alleged immigration fraud.

“I thought something was on fire,” Omar said of her initial reaction when she heard the federal agents banging on her door. “I thought something was happening to the neighbors. It sounded like an urgent evacuation sort of situation.”
She said agents “went room by room” and “took 17 items.”
The “Squad” congresswoman said her cellphones, her daughter’s old cellphone, her husband’s notebooks, a Somali phrase book and a camera were among the items taken from the home during the search.
Omar refuted reports that investigators obtained her DNA during the search.
“I would have seen if they did take anything that had contained DNA,” she said.
The congresswoman praised HSI agents for leaving the home tidy when they completed their search.
“They did a really good job in putting everything back in its place,” she said.
“They actually even folded some of my clothing that were not folded.”
Omar described the raid as “intrusive but polite.”
“They left the house in good shape.”

The probe is being led out of the Minnesota US Attorney’s Office and may involve possible false statements on immigration documents about Omar’s birth date, sources familiar with the case told The Post.
More than a dozen federal grand jury subpoenas have been issued as part of the investigation, including to relatives of Omar, the Wall Street Journal reported last week.

If the Somali-born congresswoman’s citizenship was procured by the concealment of a material fact or by willful misrepresentation — either by herself or by her father, Nur Omar Mohamed — on immigration paperwork, then the Trump administration will seek to denaturalize and deport her, a source said last week. .
Trump claims Omar could face time behind bars if she’s found to have committed immigration fraud.
“She could go to jail,” Trump said of Omar on Tuesday. “They keep talking about deportation.”
Omar has denied committing immigration fraud.
The Minnesota Democrat maintains she became a citizen at age 17 through her father, who became a naturalized citizen in 2000, five years after emigrating to the US.
A separate probe related to the congresswoman and her husband’s finances is being run out of the Washington, DC, US Attorney’s Office.
Omar has denied any wrongdoing related to her finances, as well.
“I’m confident in my truth. I’m confident in the fact that I didn’t do anything wrong,” she told Hayes.
Omar added, “I do feel confident that when it’s all said and done that I’m going to be just fine.”

articles.headline: The next Mass Effect would have had 'a level of autonomy and choice that no other game has been able to match', according to BioWare veteran
keyFacts: Former BioWare cinematic supervisor Tony de Waal said the canceled Mass Effect 4 would have featured unprecedented player autonomy and choice.
De Waal stated that about 50 people were working on the project before the studio was closed.
BioWare's closure occurred during an EA restructuring that resulted in over 400 layoffs following an acquisition.
body: A developer working on Mass Effect 4 has spoken up about BioWare's plans for the now-canceled RPG. Tony de Waal was cinematic supervisor at the now shuttered studio. He joined the team "29+ years ago", left for a spell shortly after the launch of Mass Effect 2, and then returned in 2021 to work on Dragon Age: The Veilguard. According to de Waal, there were "50-ish" people working on Mass Effect 4 before the studio closure.

"I was one of the lucky ones who stayed with BioWare to start on the next Mass Effect [after The Veilguard], where I believe we were making something special: a level of autonomy and choice that no other game has been able to match," de Waal wrote on LinkedIn.
"We saw what Larian and CD Projekt were bringing to the table with their latest offerings, and started down a path to bring Mass Effect to the next level while remaining true to the Trilogy."

De Waal also described some of the challenges BioWare faced during the development of The Veilguard, which was the studio's second project made using EA and DICE's Frostbite engine. "It was a herculean effort that tested the limits of even my workaholic mindset, and I'm proud of the level of polish we were able to pull off in the Frostbite engine.

"Seriously, you have no idea the craziness going on under the hood of that game to make a variable player character work across 3+ hours of cinematics, and the number of conditions to account for in the scenes towards the end of the game."

BioWare's closure comes as part of a big restructuring at EA following its acquisition by Saudi Arabia's PIF (and two other investment firms with tiny stakes). Over 400 people have been laid off as the publisher pivots to live service shooters and sports.

"I'm sad you won't ever get to see what we were cooking, and sad for the small, talented group of devs who were all punching above their weight to make something special," de Waal wrote. "Please consider those who stayed with BioWare until the very end. They are truly some of the most talented people I've had the pleasure of working with throughout my career."

For de Waal, as for thousands in the games industry, a hunt for work will ensue. "With that, if you need someone who knows cinematic production, blending gameplay with cinematics, the tools, the tech, and has the know-how to realize complicated narratives—a true production expert with nearly three decades of experience who isn't afraid to roll up their sleeves and create content—please think of me."
You can read de Waal's full post on LinkedIn.

With over ten years experience covering the games industry, his work has appeared on GamesRadar+, TechRadar, The Guardian, PLAY Magazine, the Sydney Morning Herald, and more. articles.headline: Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 Narrows Release Window Following Player Feedback
keyFacts: Bandai Namco announced that Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 will be released in the second half of 2027.

body: Bandai Namco announced a narrower release window for the upcoming multiplayer-enabled brawler Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3, although it's not too much more specific. Previously, the publisher had stated that the sequel to 2016 fan-favorite would arrive in 2027. Now, it's turned that from a 12-month window into a six-month one, saying that it'll be out in the second half of 2027.

"Today we shared more information about battle customization and PvE missions," producer Masayuki Hirano said. "I wanted to use this opportunity to deliver a message to our fans. Over the past several months, we have continuously revealed new information to all of you and, in return, have received valuable feedback. We are truly grateful for that support. Based on the feedback and survey results we have gathered, we have already held discussions with the development team and announced certain areas where we intend to make improvements in response.

"Dragon Ball Xenoverse is a series that we build together with the players through launch, and throughout its post launch life as well," he continued. "To fully realize our ambitions for both the launch experience and the content we plan to operate and support afterward, the release window is currently set for the latter half of 2027." He concluded by suggesting that the team might stay quiet for a while now, saying, "We may keep you waiting a little longer until our next update, but we are fully committed to making 2027 a great year for Dragon Ball game fans, and we will do everything we can to make that happen."
IGN went hands-on with Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 recently if you'd like to check out our preview impressions . Our first chance to play it was back in June.

articles.headline: AIPAC halts endorsements and direct contributions to candidates
keyFacts: AIPAC announced it will stop issuing candidate endorsements, making direct PAC contributions, and earmarking funds.
AIPAC spokesperson Deryn Sousa stated that the group will instead prioritize increasing direct, organized contributions from individual donors to candidates.
AIPAC confirmed that its affiliated super PAC, the United Democracy Project, will continue to operate and raise unlimited funds.
body: AIPAC halts endorsements and direct contributions to candidates

The pro-Israel political organization AIPAC, or the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, announced on Wednesday that it will no longer issue endorsements, make direct PAC contributions or earmark funds for candidates.

A longtime influential lobbying group, AIPAC started its direct political involvement five years ago. Since then, particularly this midterm election cycle, AIPAC has been met with mounting resistance. The group has faced criticism over its stances on various issues, including the wars in Gaza and Iran.

Candidates endorsed by AIPAC have also faced tough opposition from both the political right and the political left for accepting the organization's support and financial contributions as public opinion on the U.S. relationship with Israel has shifted. In order to tame the criticism, some AIPAC-endorsed candidates said they won't accept any money from the organization.

AIPAC first announced the changes in a letter to members, stating "the challenges we are confronting will continue to grow in the years ahead." In the letter, AIPAC said it wouldn't stop funneling money to candidates that align with the group's mission by mobilizing individual donors.

"We will prioritize increasing direct, organized contributions from individual Americans to candidates—expanding upon our current efforts—and maximizing the emerging political fundraising tools," the letter said.

The letter added that the 2028 cycle will "demand an even stronger commitment by our activists to pro-Israel politics." As a result, the group plans to increase support "for the Republicans and Democrats who are advancing policies that strengthen America's alliance with Israel and standing up against anti-Israel legislation."
In a statement to NPR, AIPAC spokesperson Deryn Sousa said the group's mission and strategy remains the same despite the changes.

"Our goal is to build support for the U.S.-Israel relationship. AIPAC members gave more than $90 million directly to candidates this cycle, and that organized, direct giving from our members will continue and increase."

AIPAC contributed nearly $25 million to candidates and political committees in 2026 through Sept. 30, according to FEC filings. Its affiliated super PAC United Democracy Project contributed $13 million to candidates and political committees and spent an additional $53.5 million in independent expenditures.

AIPAC confirmed with NPR that its affiliated super PAC, United Democracy Project, will continue to operate and will be able to raise an unlimited amount of money. It has spent heavily to support pro-Israel candidates, and oppose those who criticize Israel.
In recent days, several of the super PAC's individual independent expenditures are being used to campaign against Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan.

AIPAC also spent heavily to campaign against El-Sayed in the primary, backing his opponent, Rep. Haley Stevens. The Michigan Senate contest is just one of the high-profile races where AIPAC has spent in favor of a pro-Israel politician or in opposition to someone the organization sees as less favorable to Israel.

articles.headline: Tesla says it will start selling Cybercabs by end of year
keyFacts: Tesla announced it will start selling its autonomous Cybercab to customers by the end of the year, according to engineering vice president Lars Moravy.
Federal regulators are investigating whether the steering-wheel-free Cybercab meets vehicle safety standards that require manual controls and mirrors.
CEO Elon Musk stated that an unsupervised version of Full Self-Driving for existing Tesla owners will be rolled out in the second quarter of next year.
body: Tesla said Wednesday it will start selling its Cybercab to customers by the end of the year, even as federal regulators investigate whether the vehicle meets vehicle safety standards. The gold-hued, autonomous two-seater lacks a steering wheel and other traditional controls.

During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Lars Moravy, vice president of engineering at Tesla, said the Cybercabs produced today are all destined for the company’s own robotaxi fleet. As that fleet grows, the company will “mainly deliver fully designed autonomous vehicles to our customers,” he said, noting that it will start small. The company will scale as it learns about delivery, ownership, and fleet management of autonomous vehicles, Moravy added.

Tesla first floated the idea of selling the autonomous vehicle to third parties last month around its Cybercab event in Austin and even posted a form for people interested in buying robotaxis. But it wasn’t clear if Tesla would follow through, or how.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk has talked for years about building a massive fleet of low-cost robotaxis, but until recently, those plans centered on turning privately owned Tesla vehicles into self-driving taxis with a software update.
That plan has yet to materialize, and Musk’s comments on the call show how his views have shifted.

Today, Tesla owners can subscribe to Full Self-Driving (Supervised), an advanced driver-assistance system that automates many driving tasks but still requires the driver to take control. The company continues to push out software updates to the system to improve its capabilities, but a human driver is still required to remain engaged and ready to take over — even though many videos show drivers testing the limits of that rule.

Musk said Wednesday that an unsupervised version of FSD, the fully self-driving version, would be rolled out to customers sometime in the second quarter of next year, yet another delay for Tesla owners, many of whom bought or subscribed to the software years ago.

If both timelines hold, it would mean third-party fleet customers would be able to buy the autonomous Cybercab and potentially operate it as a robotaxi service before Tesla owners would get access to the same autonomous capability in their own cars.

Musk said the Cybercab is meant to be a ride-hailing vehicle, not a car people own. “Cybercab is primarily going to be something that is offered as like transport as a service, whereas our other cars would be more, you know, the cars that you’d want to own, like the 3 and the Y and whatnot, and the Roadster, obviously,” Musk said Wednesday on the call. “But, you know, the vast majority of the Cybercab stuff will be essentially Tesla-owned and transported as a service.”

There is at least one obstacle that could throw off Tesla’s Cybercab fleet plans. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), the federal auto safety regulator, announced last month that it had opened an investigation into the Cybercab, just hours after the vehicles began operating on public streets in Austin.

Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (FMVSS) require manual controls like brake pedals, as well as other features such as rearview and side mirrors. Automakers traditionally self-certify whether their vehicles comply with FMVSS rules, and Tesla did the same.

Current regulations don’t accommodate vehicles without manual controls, though the Department of Transportation recently proposed removing those requirements for vehicles that are designed to be autonomously driven. In the meantime, NHTSA said it would investigate the Cybercab to “examine the process and technical data on which Tesla relied when certifying the Cybercab and related issues.”
The outcome of that investigation could affect whether Tesla, or anyone else, can legally operate the Cybercab.

articles.headline: YouTube says it isn’t testing hiding the dislike button
keyFacts: YouTube spokesperson Kimberly Taylor stated that the company is not testing hiding the dislike button for regular users.
